title: Minimum Spanning Trees
summary: Connecting everything as cheaply as possible - spanning trees, the cut property that makes greedy choices safe, Kruskal's algorithm with sorting and union-find, Prim's algorithm with a priority queue, the dense O(V^2) version of Prim for complete graphs, minimum spanning forests, and uses from network design to clustering.

cards.q: Why does a minimum spanning tree never contain a cycle?
cards.a:
Dropping a cycle's costliest edge is cheaper

Removing the most expensive edge of a cycle keeps everything connected and lowers the cost.

cards.q: In Kruskal's algorithm, what does union-find decide?
cards.a:
Whether an edge would close a cycle

It tells whether the edge's two ends are already connected; `unite(a, b)` returning false means they are in the same tree.

cards.q: How does Prim's priority differ from Dijkstra's?
cards.a:
It is one edge's cost, not a path length

A vertex's priority in Prim is the cost of the single edge attaching it to the tree; Dijkstra uses the total distance from the start.
